items.title: Opening a coding round clearly
items.instruction: Practice a 30-second opener: restate the problem, confirm inputs/outputs, ask one clarifying question, and state your high-level approach before typing.
items.practicePrompt: Record yourself opening Two Sum or a similar easy problem. Attempt without AI first; then compare to a senior engineer sample for pacing only.
items.youtubeSearch: Google coding interview communication think aloud

items.title: Clarifying ambiguous requirements
items.instruction: Use phrases like 'Can we assume…', 'Should I optimize for time or memory?', and 'What should happen if the input is empty?'
items.practicePrompt: Take an underspecified LeetCode medium; write three clarifying questions before coding. No AI until after your list is done.
items.youtubeSearch: coding interview clarifying questions examples

items.title: Think-aloud while coding
items.instruction: Narrate invariants, loop purpose, and why you chose a data structure. Silence longer than 20 seconds should trigger you to explain what you are thinking.
items.practicePrompt: Solve Valid Parentheses out loud with a timer. Attempt solo first; use AI only to critique clarity, not to generate code.
items.youtubeSearch: Google coding interview think aloud example

items.title: Recovering from a bug mid-interview
items.instruction: Say 'Let me trace an example' or 'I suspect an off-by-one here' instead of panicking. Verbalize your debug plan.
items.practicePrompt: Introduce a deliberate bug in your solution, then practice fixing it on camera with continuous narration. Attempt without AI first.
items.youtubeSearch: debugging out loud coding interview

items.title: Explaining time and space complexity
items.instruction: Template: 'We visit each element once…', 'The map holds at most n…', 'Recursion depth is…'. Tie Big-O to the code lines.
items.practicePrompt: After solving Merge Intervals, give a 60-second complexity analysis. Record and review before any AI feedback.
items.youtubeSearch: big O explanation interview concise

items.title: System design opening script
items.instruction: Start with users, core use cases, scale assumptions, then API sketch before deep diving components.
items.practicePrompt: Open a URL shortener design for five minutes on whiteboard or paper. Attempt without AI first; then check against a reference outline.
items.youtubeSearch: Google system design interview how to start

items.title: Trade-off language for design
items.instruction: Use 'We gain X at the cost of Y' and 'At our scale, Z matters more because…'
items.practicePrompt: Compare SQL vs NoSQL for a news feed read path in spoken form (3 minutes). Solo attempt first.
items.youtubeSearch: system design tradeoffs explained

items.title: STAR-L: Leadership on a hard deadline
items.instruction: Situation, Task, Action, Result, Learnings. Keep Actions specific (you did X, not 'we tried'). Learnings show growth without blaming others.
items.practicePrompt: Draft one story about unblocking a team under deadline pressure. Write bullets first without AI; polish wording after.
items.youtubeSearch: STAR method software engineer Google interview

items.title: STAR-L: Technical disagreement
items.instruction: Show data, respect for peers, and outcome—even if your idea was not chosen.
items.practicePrompt: Prepare a story where you disagreed on architecture or implementation. Emphasize how you validated assumptions.
items.youtubeSearch: behavioral interview conflict technical decision Google

items.title: STAR-L: Mistake and accountability
items.instruction: Google expects ownership: what broke, how you detected it, how you fixed and prevented recurrence.
items.practicePrompt: Write a production incident or serious bug story with measurable Result. Attempt without AI first.
items.youtubeSearch: tell me about a failure interview answer engineer

items.title: STAR-L: Mentoring or lifting others
items.instruction: Focus on the other person's growth and concrete steps you took (pairing, docs, feedback).
items.practicePrompt: Prepare a story about helping a junior or cross-functional partner succeed. Time to 3 minutes spoken.
items.youtubeSearch: behavioral interview mentoring software engineer

items.title: STAR-L: Ambiguity and prioritization
items.instruction: Describe unclear requirements, how you narrowed scope, and who you aligned with.
items.practicePrompt: Story about a project with shifting goals. Highlight customer or user impact in Result.
items.youtubeSearch: ambiguous project behavioral interview Google

items.title: Googleyness: Help others succeed
items.instruction: Prepare examples where you shared credit, unblocked others, or improved team processes without being asked.
items.practicePrompt: List three situations; pick the strongest for a 2-minute answer. No AI until draft exists.
items.youtubeSearch: Googleyness help others succeed interview

items.title: Googleyness: Thriving in ambiguity
items.instruction: Show comfort defining the problem, not only executing a spec.
items.practicePrompt: Answer 'Tell me about a time requirements were unclear' using your STAR-L draft from com012.
items.youtubeSearch: Google interview ambiguity example

items.title: Googleyness: Doing the right thing
items.instruction: Ethics, privacy, security, or pushing back on harmful shortcuts—done respectfully with business context.
items.practicePrompt: Prepare one story about integrity or user trust. Avoid confidential details; use anonymized facts.
items.youtubeSearch: Google behavioral doing the right thing

items.title: Googleyness: Customer / user focus
items.instruction: Tie technical work to user-visible outcomes or metrics when possible.
items.practicePrompt: Rewrite a past project summary to lead with user impact, then technical approach (90 seconds).
items.youtubeSearch: software engineer user focus behavioral

items.title: Wrapping a coding solution
items.instruction: Walk through a test case, mention edge cases handled, and optional optimizations you would explore with more time.
items.practicePrompt: After any medium solve, practice a 90-second walkthrough. Record; fix unclear phrases before AI review.
items.youtubeSearch: coding interview wrap up test cases

items.title: Asking good questions at the end
items.instruction: Ask about team impact, on-call, tech stack evolution, or mentorship—not perks only.
items.practicePrompt: Write five questions for a Google SWE team. Attempt without searching sample lists first.
items.youtubeSearch: questions to ask interviewer Google engineer

items.title: Explaining Go concurrency choices
items.instruction: When discussing goroutines, state why channels vs mutex, and mention context cancellation.
items.practicePrompt: Explain a worker-pool design aloud for 3 minutes as if to an interviewer. Attempt without AI first.
items.youtubeSearch: explain goroutines channels interview

items.title: STAR-L: Cross-functional collaboration
items.instruction: Include PM, design, or other eng roles; show communication and compromise.
items.practicePrompt: Draft story with a non-engineer stakeholder. Keep jargon minimal in the spoken version.
items.youtubeSearch: cross functional collaboration STAR story

items.title: Handling 'Tell me about yourself'
items.instruction: 2–3 minute arc: present role, relevant highlights, why Google/this team, forward-looking hook.
items.practicePrompt: Write and rehearse TMAY three times with a timer. Critique yourself before optional AI polish.
items.youtubeSearch: tell me about yourself software engineer Google

items.title: Googleyness: Innovation and simplicity
items.instruction: Show when you simplified a system or chose a boring technology for reliability.
items.practicePrompt: Prepare one example of deliberate simplification with before/after impact.
items.youtubeSearch: Googleyness innovation simplicity interview

items.title: Pairing-style narration
items.instruction: Invite feedback: 'Does this approach sound reasonable?' while staying driver of the solution.
items.practicePrompt: Mock with a friend or record both sides; practice checkpoint questions every 5 minutes.
items.youtubeSearch: pair programming interview communication Google

items.title: STAR-L: Learning something new quickly
items.instruction: Demonstrate structured learning: docs, spikes, prototypes, validation.
items.practicePrompt: Story about picking up a new language, framework, or domain under time pressure.
items.youtubeSearch: learn new technology quickly behavioral interview

items.title: Googleyness: Feedback and growth
items.instruction: Give an example of receiving tough feedback and changing behavior with measurable follow-through.
items.practicePrompt: Write 2-minute answer; avoid sounding defensive. Attempt solo first.
items.youtubeSearch: receive feedback behavioral interview engineer

items.title: Google Careers: How we hire overview
items.instruction: Read Google's public hiring pages and note how coding, system design, and Googleyness/Leadership are evaluated. Write a one-page prep map for your timeline.
items.practicePrompt: After reading, list three behaviors Google says they look for and map each to one of your STAR stories. Attempt without AI first.
items.youtubeSearch: Google how we hire software engineer

items.title: Watch: Google coding interview communication
items.instruction: Watch a public Google-style coding interview and pause every 5 minutes to note how the candidate clarifies, narrates, and recovers from mistakes.
items.practicePrompt: Write five 'I will copy this' communication behaviors and one 'I will avoid this'. Rehearse one behavior on your next LeetCode solve.
items.youtubeSearch: Google coding interview full example think aloud

items.title: Behavioral deep-dive: Googleyness playlist drill
items.instruction: Pick three public Google behavioral / Googleyness tip videos. For each, extract one rubric phrase and attach it to a STAR-L bullet in your story bank.
items.practicePrompt: Deliver three 2-minute STAR answers on camera. Self-score clarity, ownership, and impact before any AI feedback.
items.youtubeSearch: Googleyness Leadership interview questions software engineer

items.title: Google SWE: end-to-end mock communication
items.instruction: Run a 45-minute mock: 5 min TMAY + Googleyness, 25 min coding with think-aloud, 10 min wrap + questions for interviewer. Use only public Google careers guidance as the rubric.
items.practicePrompt: Record or pair with a friend. Score yourself on opener, clarifying questions, narration density, and closing questions. Attempt without AI until after the mock.
items.youtubeSearch: Google software engineer mock interview communication

items.title: Why Google / why this team (spoken)
items.instruction: Build a sincere 90-second answer: product/user impact you care about, how your skills fit, and one concrete question about the team's work. Avoid generic praise.
items.practicePrompt: Write then speak the answer three times. Cut fluff until it fits under 90 seconds. Solo attempt first.
items.youtubeSearch: why Google interview answer software engineer
